title: Information systems and IT
blurb: Spreadsheets, databases, accounting software and networks.

topics.name: What is an information system?
topics.line: Collect, store, produce and distribute information.
topics.remember: Information systems = all systems and procedures for collecting, storing, producing and distributing information. Tools: spreadsheets, databases, accounting packages, networks.
topics.simple: An information system is every system and procedure a business uses to collect, store, make and share information.
frames: Storage: it is kept in a database.
Production: it is processed into reports.
Distribution: reports reach the people who need them.
gls: all systems and procedures for collection, storage, production and distribution
connected devices sharing information and resources

topics.name: Spreadsheets
topics.line: Cells hold text, values, formulae and functions.
topics.remember: Cell A4 = column A, row 4. Formula: =B4+B5. Function: =SUM(B4:B10). Spreadsheets are for flexible analysis.
topics.simple: A spreadsheet is a grid of cells. Each cell has a name made from its column and row, and holds one of four kinds of content.
frames: Column A and row 4 meet at cell A4.
Text is words, such as a column header.
A formula such as =B4+B5 adds two cells.
A function such as =SUM(B4:B10) is a ready-made formula.
gls: one box, named by column and row
an expression you write to calculate a value
a predefined formula built into the application

cards.mean: Usually words, or numbers that are not values for calculation
A number that can be used in a calculation
An expression that calculates the value of a cell, usually referencing other cells
cards.ex: =B4+B5 adds the values in B4 and B5.

cards.mean: Predefined formulae built into the application: arithmetical, financial and statistical
cards.ex: =SUM(B4:B10) adds all values from B4 to B10.

caps: Columns are lettered (A, B). Rows are numbered (1, 2, 3).

topics.name: Database systems
topics.line: Structured and unstructured data, and where a database lives.
topics.remember: Structured: defined fields and tables. Unstructured: text, audio, video. Small: local file system. Large: servers or cloud.
topics.simple: A database stores and manages data so users can get it in a useful form. Big ones need bigger homes.
frames: Structured data sits in defined fields and tables, like financial records.
Unstructured data is files such as text, audio and video.
A small database can sit on a local file system.
A large database needs servers or cloud.

topics.name: Computer networks
topics.line: Five advantages and four network types.
topics.remember: LAN: short distance, cables. WAN: wide area, connects LANs. WLAN: wireless, radio. VPN: encrypted, any distance.
topics.simple: A network connects two or more devices so they can exchange information and share resources. Types differ by coverage.
frames: LAN: short distance, such as one building, usually cables.
WLAN: like a LAN, but by radio with no cables.
WAN: a region or country, connecting many LANs.
VPN: an encrypted connection over the internet, any distance.
gls: two or more devices connected to exchange information and resources
